label: QBO to CSV
summary: Extract transaction rows from a QBO bank feed file into a clean CSV you can inspect or edit.
detail: Read bank STMTTRN entries, preserve dates, amounts, payee descriptions and available transaction IDs. This is a read-only export; bank configuration metadata is not recreated.
faq: Does this change the original bank file?
answer: No. Your original QBO file is read locally and never modified or uploaded.

label: QBO to Excel
summary: Turn QBO bank feed transactions into an editable Excel spreadsheet, entirely in your browser.
detail: Export a proper .xlsx workbook with date, description, signed amount and reference columns. Investment feeds and accounting splits are outside this reader's scope.
faq: Is the download a real Excel workbook?
answer: Yes. The application generates an .xlsx workbook locally. It is not just a CSV renamed with an Excel extension.

label: QIF to CSV
summary: Export bank-style QIF transaction records to CSV without creating an account.
detail: Read QIF D/T/P/M/N bank fields, review the result and export. QIF split categories and investment records are not reproduced.
answer: Basic bank-like QIF transactions with date and amount fields. Split and investment details are not carried into the output.

label: QIF to Excel
summary: Make a readable Excel transaction sheet from a QIF bank export.
detail: Convert basic QIF transactions to four consistent spreadsheet columns. Verify dates and signed amounts in the preview before downloading.
faq: Will I lose split transaction detail?
answer: Yes. This release exports basic transaction rows only and clearly warns when split/category fields are encountered.

label: IIF to CSV
summary: Inspect the main transaction rows of a QuickBooks IIF export as CSV.
detail: Reads !TRNS/TRNS entries from supported IIF tab-delimited files. It is not a full double-entry ledger export and must not be used as an accounting migration substitute.
faq: Can I reconstruct all journal entries?
answer: No. SPL and account allocations are not reconstructed, so the export is only a summary-row inspection tool.

label: IIF to Excel
summary: View supported IIF transaction summary rows in an Excel worksheet.
detail: For IIF files containing a !TRNS header, extracts the main date, amount, memo and reference fields. Accounting splits are intentionally not reconstructed.
faq: Can I import this Excel file back into QuickBooks Desktop?
answer: No import compatibility is claimed. This export is for inspection only.

label: OFX to CSV
summary: Read an OFX bank transaction file and download a clean CSV extract.
detail: Supports common OFX 1.x and XML-style STMTTRN bank transaction blocks. Investment and unusual bank variants require further testing.
faq: Does the converter contact my bank?
answer: No. It reads a file you already have. No credentials or bank connections are requested.

label: OFX to Excel
summary: Export OFX bank transactions to a structured Excel workbook.
detail: For supported OFX bank feeds, exports posted date, payee name, signed amount and FITID transaction reference into .xlsx.
faq: Can it read investment OFX files?
answer: Not in this release. It requires standard bank STMTTRN records.

label: QFX to Excel
summary: Extract QFX bank transaction data into a useful Excel spreadsheet.
detail: Read the standard STMTTRN section of a Quicken QFX bank export. Financial institution identity and account metadata are not transferred to Excel.
faq: Does it alter my Quicken file?
answer: No. Your QFX stays unchanged in your browser. This is a read-only extraction.

label: QFX to CSV
summary: Export supported QFX bank feed transactions to a portable CSV format.
detail: Only standard STMTTRN bank transaction records are supported. Search demand for this exact page has not been validated.
faq: Is this an official Quicken converter?
answer: No. This is an independent file-reading utility, not affiliated with Quicken or Intuit.

label: QuickBooks CSV Formatter
summary: Clean and standardize a CSV transaction list into a three-column file for the QuickBooks Online manual CSV upload workflow.
detail: Choose date, description and amount columns. Format and preview the data before saving a fresh CSV. This does not generate a QBO Web Connect file and is not proof of a successful QuickBooks import.
answer: No. It creates a three-column CSV for manual upload and field mapping in QuickBooks Online. Import success depends on the receiving account.

label: CSV to QIF (Preview)
summary: Map a CSV bank transaction list and generate a basic QIF Bank file for testing.
detail: QIF output structure is validated locally, but actual importing into individual finance software versions is not verified. Do not use this for production accounting without testing.
answer: No. The file is syntax-checked, but target software import behavior has not been independently validated.
